title: 551. The Road to 1066: Countdown to Conquest (Part 4)

sentences.en: Harold, eldest in birth as in wisdom, was by the king's favour appointed to the earldom in his father's place.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德，无论在出生还是智慧上都是长子，承蒙国王恩宠，接替了他父亲的伯爵之位。

sentences.en: In the strength of his body and mind, he stood forth among the people as a second Judas Maccabeus, a true friend of his people and his country.
sentences.zh: 他身心强健，在民众中脱颖而出，宛如第二位犹大·马加比，是他的人民和国家的真正挚友。

sentences.en: He wielded his father's powers even more actively and walked in his ways, that is, in patience and mercy and with kindness to men of goodwill.
sentences.zh: 他比父亲更积极地行使权力，并遵循父亲的道路，即以耐心、仁慈和善意对待心怀善念之人。

sentences.en: But disturbers of the peace, thieves and robbers, this champion of the law, threatened with the terrible face of our lion.
sentences.zh: 但对于那些破坏和平者、窃贼和强盗，这位法律的捍卫者以我们狮子般威严的面孔威胁他们。

sentences.en: Well practised he was in endless fatigues and doing without sleep and food, and endowed with mildness of temper and a more ready understanding.
sentences.zh: 他极其擅长应对无尽的劳苦，能忍受睡眠和饮食的匮乏，且天性温和，理解力超群。

sentences.en: He could bear contradiction well, not readily revealing or retaliating, never, I think, on a fellow citizen or compatriot.
sentences.zh: 他善于承受异议，不会轻易显露不满或进行报复，我想，他绝不会对同胞或国人这样做。

sentences.en: Indeed, the fault of rashness or levity is not one that anybody could charge against him.
sentences.zh: 事实上，鲁莽或轻浮的过错，谁也无法归咎于他。

sentences.en: Sir Tom Holland, the name of this paragon, this patriotic icon.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰德爵士，这位楷模、这位爱国偶像的名字。

sentences.en: Dominic Sandbrook.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克·桑德布鲁克。

sentences.en: This hero, this enduring hero of the English people, a man worthy to stand as England's last true-born king.
sentences.zh: 这位英雄，这位英国人民心中永恒的英雄，一个足以作为英格兰最后一位纯正血统国王的人。

sentences.en: It is, of course, Harold Godwinson, Earl of Wessex, the man who falls at the Battle of Hastings.
sentences.zh: 当然，他就是威塞克斯伯爵哈罗德·戈德温森，那个在黑斯廷斯战役中阵亡的人。

sentences.en: And last time we were talking about Duke William of Normandy, the villain of this story.
sentences.zh: 上次我们谈到了诺曼底公爵威廉，这个故事里的反派。

sentences.en: And today we're on somebody who I've always...
sentences.zh: 而今天我们要讲的是一个我一直……

sentences.en: Held a candle for.
sentences.zh: 一直很欣赏的人。

sentences.en: Held a candle for, exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 一直很欣赏，没错，确实如此。

sentences.en: Do you see yourself reflected in his character?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他的性格中有你的影子吗？

sentences.en: And his prowess?
sentences.zh: 还有他的英勇？

sentences.en: The terrible face of a lion, endowed with mildness of temper and a ready understanding.
sentences.zh: 狮子般威严的面孔，天性温和，理解力超群。

sentences.en: He could bear contradiction well.
sentences.zh: 他善于承受异议。

sentences.en: I mean, it's all adding up.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这一切都对上了。

sentences.en: It's all there, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 都在这儿了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's uncanny.
sentences.zh: 是的，太不可思议了。

sentences.en: It's uncanny.
sentences.zh: 太不可思议了。

sentences.en: So this is actually from a biography of Edward the Confessor, not of Harold.
sentences.zh: 所以这其实是出自《忏悔者爱德华传》，而不是哈罗德的传记。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Harold is a supporting character in this book.
sentences.zh: 所以哈罗德在这本书里只是个配角。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A lot of what we know about the reign of Edward, who was crowned at the end of the last episode and goes on to be called the Confessor.
sentences.zh: 我们对爱德华统治时期的了解，很多都来自这本书。他在上一集结尾加冕，后来被称为“忏悔者”。

sentences.en: Not because he's rushing around confessing to things all the time, which is what people often think.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为他总是到处向人忏悔，人们常这么以为。

sentences.en: It's because there are multiple Edwards and people haven't yet worked out that you could call them the first, the second, the third or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 而是因为当时叫爱德华的人太多了，人们还没想出用第一、第二、第三这种方式来区分他们。

sentences.en: I think this is a much better way of doing it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这种方式好多了。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: So Alfred the Great's son was called Edward.
sentences.zh: 阿尔弗雷德大帝的儿子叫爱德华。

sentences.en: So he's Edward the Elder.
sentences.zh: 所以他是长者爱德华。

sentences.en: And then we had Edward the Martyr.
sentences.zh: 然后是殉道者爱德华。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Edward the Confessor is someone who is a saint, but hasn't been martyred, basically.
sentences.zh: 而忏悔者爱德华是个圣人，但基本上并没有殉道。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Or that bloke, Harold Harefoot.
sentences.zh: 或者那个叫“兔足”哈罗德的家伙。

sentences.en: I mean, if you make up a nickname later, if necessary.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果有必要，以后再编个绰号也行。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: But that passage that you read comes from a life of Edward the Confessor.
sentences.zh: 但你刚才读的那段话出自《忏悔者爱德华传》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Probably written in the immediate aftermath of his death early in 1066 and almost certainly commissioned by his queen, who is a woman called Edith.
sentences.zh: 很可能写于1066年初他去世后的第一时间，而且几乎可以肯定是由他的王后，一个叫伊迪丝的女人委托撰写的。

sentences.en: And who just happens to be the sister of Harold.
sentences.zh: 而她恰好是哈罗德的妹妹。

sentences.en: So you can see that this is certain.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出这肯定是……

sentences.en: I think these are pretty objective people, to be fair.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我觉得这些人相当客观。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, you say that, except that Harold is not the only member of his family to be praised in the life of King Edward, because there is also his younger brother, Tostig Godwinson.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你这么说，但哈罗德并不是《爱德华国王传》中唯一受到赞扬的家族成员，因为书中还提到了他的弟弟，托斯蒂·戈德温森。

sentences.en: And Tostig, like Harold, is an earl.
sentences.zh: 而且托斯蒂和哈罗德一样，也是一位伯爵。

sentences.en: And he's described in the life of King Edward as a man endowed with very great and prudent restraint.
sentences.zh: 在《爱德华国王传》中，他被描述为一个拥有伟大而审慎的克制力的人。

sentences.en: Although occasionally he was a little overzealous in attacking evil and with bold and inflexible constancy of mind.
sentences.zh: 尽管偶尔他在打击邪恶时显得过于热心，且意志坚定、毫不动摇。

sentences.en: And we will see in due course today whether that is a fair description or not.
sentences.zh: 我们今天稍后会看看这种描述是否公允。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we're talking today about this family, the Godwinsons, who we left out of the previous episodes because we wanted to do them all today.
sentences.zh: 所以我们今天讨论的是戈德温森家族，我们在之前的剧集中略过了他们，因为我们想把他们放在今天集中讲。

sentences.en: And they're obviously massive players in the story of 1066, because we've already had three members of the family.
sentences.zh: 他们显然是1066年故事中的重量级人物，因为我们已经提到了家族中的三位成员。

sentences.en: We've had Harold, we've had Tostig, and we have had Edith.
sentences.zh: 我们提到了哈罗德、托斯蒂和伊迪丝。

sentences.en: And behind them, hence the name Godwinson, is this bloke, Godwin, who is not massively well known, I would say, in English history today,
sentences.zh: 而在他们身后，也就是“戈德温森”这个名字的由来，是这个叫戈德温的家伙。我觉得他在今天的英国历史上并不广为人知，

sentences.en: but is a titanic figure in English history in the 11th century.
sentences.zh: 但他却是11世纪英国历史上的一位泰斗级人物。

sentences.en: So tell us a bit about Godwin and why his name carries such significance to people in the 11th century.
sentences.zh: 那么给我们讲讲戈德温，以及为什么他的名字在11世纪的人们心中具有如此重要的意义。

sentences.en: Well, he is an astonishing example of social mobility.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他是社会流动性的一个惊人例子。

sentences.en: And he's a classic example of how in periods of chaos and change and disaster for lots of people, some can find opportunity.
sentences.zh: 他是那种在混乱、变革和灾难时期，有些人如何能找到机遇的典型案例。

sentences.en: And so to look at how he emerges to this astonishing position of predominance in England, we need to go back to 1016, the conquest of England by Canute and the Danes.
sentences.zh: 要了解他是如何崛起并达到英国这种惊人的统治地位的，我们需要回到1016年，克努特大帝和丹麦人征服英国的时候。

sentences.en: And the consequence of Canute's triumph is not just the toppling of the Kurdik ingas, the traditional ruling West Saxon dynasty,
sentences.zh: 克努特胜利的后果不仅是推翻了传统的西撒克逊统治王朝，

sentences.en: but also the replacement of large numbers of English eldermen, the guys who are in charge of the kind of the various counties and regions in England,
sentences.zh: 还用丹麦的“雅尔”或后来英语化的“伯爵”，取代了大量的英国地方长官，也就是那些负责英国各郡和地区的人，

sentences.en: by Danish jarls or earls as they come to be anglicised.
sentences.zh: （接上句）也就是那些负责英国各郡和地区的人。

sentences.en: But there is one Englishman who is appointed to a position of high rank by Canute early in his reign.
sentences.zh: 但有一位英国人在克努特统治初期就被任命为高官。

sentences.en: And I'm quoting here from the life of King Edward, a man judged by the king, most cautious in council and active in war.
sentences.zh: 我引用《爱德华国王传》中的话：“一位被国王评价为在议政时最谨慎、在战争中极活跃的人。”

sentences.en: And this is Godwin, who is simply an obscure thane from Sussex.
sentences.zh: 这就是戈德温，他当时只是萨塞克斯郡一个默默无闻的领主。

sentences.en: He has no real pedigree at all.
sentences.zh: 他根本没有任何真正的家世背景。

sentences.en: And in fact, his father had been arraigned by Æthelred on a charge we're not sure exactly what.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他的父亲曾被埃塞尔雷德指控，具体罪名我们不确定。

sentences.en: Um, and he's very cross about this and he commandeers 20 ships from Æthelred's fleet and basically he kind of turns Viking.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他对此非常愤怒，于是从埃塞尔雷德的舰队中强征了20艘船，基本上算是当了海盗。

sentences.en: He goes off kind of raiding the south coast of England.
sentences.zh: 他开始在英格兰南海岸进行劫掠。

sentences.en: And it may be that this is how Godwin meets Canute, that because he's essentially turned Viking, maybe he meets the real Vikings.
sentences.zh: 戈德温可能就是这样遇见克努特的，因为他本质上已经成了海盗，也许他遇见了真正的维京人。

sentences.en: Maybe Canute recognises a kindred spirit.
sentences.zh: 也许克努特认出了志同道合的人。

sentences.en: But certainly once Canute has become king, Godwin's rise is astonishingly rapid.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，一旦克努特成为国王，戈德温的崛起速度就惊人地快。

sentences.en: So in 1020, Canute, who up until that point had been serving as Earl of Wessex himself, you know, he's got a large empire to rule.
sentences.zh: 所以到了1020年，克努特，他之前一直亲自担任威塞克斯伯爵，你知道，他还要统治一个庞大的帝国。

sentences.en: So he doesn't really want to shoulder that burden.
sentences.zh: 所以他其实不想承担那个重担。

sentences.en: So he gives it to Godwin, who becomes Earl of Wessex.
sentences.zh: 于是他把这个职位给了戈德温，戈德温因此成为了威塞克斯伯爵。

sentences.en: Also, he marries him to his own sister-in-law, a Danish woman called Gither.
sentences.zh: 此外，他还将自己的小姨子，一位名叫吉莎的丹麦女子嫁给了他。

sentences.en: And in consequence of that, you called Harold the last true-born king of England.
sentences.zh: 因此，你称哈罗德为英格兰最后一位纯正血统的国王。

sentences.en: But I mean, he is half Danish.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，他有一半丹麦血统。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: As is Tostig, as is Edith.
sentences.zh: 托斯蒂也是，伊迪丝也是。

sentences.en: So we think of them as the embodiments of Anglo-Saxon England, I guess, because they're ruling and living in the twilight of Anglo-Saxon England.
sentences.zh: 我想我们把他们视为盎格鲁-撒克逊英格兰的化身，因为他们生活在盎格鲁-撒克逊英格兰的黄昏时期并进行统治。

sentences.en: But they are also evidence of the way in which England is an inextricable part of the Danish world as well.
sentences.zh: 但他们也证明了英格兰与丹麦世界有着不可分割的联系。

sentences.en: So in that sense, I guess they are really good embodiments of Anglo-Saxon England, because, of course, for centuries, Anglo-Saxon England has had a huge Danish component to it.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，我想他们确实是盎格鲁-撒克逊英格兰很好的化身，因为几个世纪以来，盎格鲁-撒克逊英格兰一直包含着巨大的丹麦成分。

sentences.en: Hence the place names and, you know, the people's personal names and the Thor's hammers and all of those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 看看地名、人们的个人名字、雷神之锤等等这些东西就知道了。

sentences.en: So just on Godwin, you could say about Godwin, yes, he's a symbol of upward mobility.
sentences.zh: 所以单就戈德温而言，你可以说，是的，他是社会向上流动的象征。

sentences.en: He's also a symbol of collaboration with an occupier.
sentences.zh: 他也是与占领者合作的象征。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it works for him because by the time Canute dies in 1035, he is indisputably the most powerful magnate in the kingdom.
sentences.zh: 这对他是有效的，因为到1035年克努特去世时，他无疑是王国中最强大的权贵。

sentences.en: I mean, he is a figure whose support is key for anyone who wants to rule as king.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他的支持对于任何想当国王的人来说都是关键。

sentences.en: And it is evidence of, you know, these powers of resourcefulness, of prudence, of opportunism, of charm that the life of King Edward alludes to.
sentences.zh: 这证明了《爱德华国王传》所提到的那些足智多谋、审慎、投机和魅力。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is essentially his own daughter praising him.
sentences.zh: 而且，这本质上是他自己的女儿在赞美他。

sentences.en: But clearly the proof of these qualities is the fact that he's able to survive the shipwreck of Athelred's fortunes, profit from them,
sentences.zh: 但显然，这些品质的证明在于他能够从埃塞尔雷德财富的沉船中幸存下来，从中获利，

sentences.en: and then survive this kind of seesaw chain of succession with Canute, his two sons, and then Edward.
sentences.zh: 然后在克努特、他的两个儿子以及爱德华之间这种摇摆不定的继位链中生存下来。

sentences.en: So Godwin shows an unbelievable talent for swimming with the tide.
sentences.zh: 所以戈德温展现了令人难以置信的顺应时势的天赋。

sentences.en: So first of all, he backs Emma and Arthur Canute in the wake of Canute's death.
sentences.zh: 首先，在克努特死后，他支持了艾玛和哈瑟克努特。

sentences.en: Then when it's clear that Harold Harefoot is going to be king, he switches sides.
sentences.zh: 然后当“兔足”哈罗德显然要成为国王时，他倒戈了。

sentences.en: When Alfred, Emma's son by Athelred, lands, and people who listened to our previous episode will remember that Alfred gets seized along with his retinue.
sentences.zh: 当艾玛和埃塞尔雷德的儿子阿尔弗雷德登陆时，听过我们上一集的人会记得阿尔弗雷德和他的随从被抓住了。

sentences.en: They all get kind of scalped, blinded, chained up, whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们都被剥了头皮、弄瞎了眼睛、锁了起来，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And Alfred himself is blinded and dies of his wounds.
sentences.zh: 阿尔弗雷德本人被弄瞎了眼睛，最终伤重不治。

sentences.en: The guy who is responsible for this is Godwin.
sentences.zh: 对此负责的人就是戈德温。

sentences.en: It is Godwin who supervises essentially the kind of the slaughter of Alfred and his retinue and supervises the guy who is the brother of Edward, who is going to become king,
sentences.zh: 正是戈德温监督了对阿尔弗雷德及其随从的屠杀，并监督了爱德华（未来的国王）的兄弟，

sentences.en: his blinding in Ely.
sentences.zh: 在伊利被弄瞎双眼的过程。

sentences.en: And then when Arthur Canute becomes king, Godwin very smoothly moves back to serving him.
sentences.zh: 然后当哈瑟克努特成为国王时，戈德温又非常圆滑地转回去侍奉他。

sentences.en: But his most startling switchback is still to come because it is Godwin who plays the leading role in finessing the restoration of the original West Saxon ruling line to the English throne in the form of Edward the Confessor.
sentences.zh: 但他最令人震惊的转折还在后面，因为正是戈德温在促成西撒克逊原始统治血统以忏悔者爱德华的形式重返英格兰王位中发挥了主导作用。

sentences.en: And just to reiterate, it's startling partly because Godwin has inherited this grudge from his father against Athelred.
sentences.zh: 重申一下，这之所以令人震惊，部分原因是戈德温继承了他父亲对埃塞尔雷德的怨恨。

sentences.en: More obviously, because his entire status as the most powerful magnate in England entirely derives from Danish rule and from the fact that Athelred's family have been expelled.
sentences.zh: 更明显的是，他作为英格兰最强大权贵的全部地位完全源于丹麦统治，源于埃塞尔雷德家族被驱逐的事实。

sentences.en: And above all, I guess, because he's the guy who blinded and essentially killed Edward's brother.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，我想，因为他就是那个弄瞎并实质上杀害了爱德华兄弟的人。

sentences.en: But maybe there's an explanation for this, which is that Edward, as we will discuss, has been in Normandy for the great majority of his adult life.
sentences.zh: 但也许对此有一个解释，那就是爱德华，正如我们将要讨论的那样，他成年后的大部分时间都在诺曼底度过。

sentences.en: So he doesn't have the affinity, the connections, the networks in England.
sentences.zh: 所以他在英格兰没有那种亲缘关系、人脉和网络。

sentences.en: Whereas Godwin, he may hate Godwin and he may think, you know,
sentences.zh: 而戈德温，他可能讨厌戈德温，他可能心想，你知道，

sentences.en: I think it's completely reasonable that you might have a grudge against somebody who blinded and mutilated your brother.
sentences.zh: 我觉得对一个弄瞎并残害了你兄弟的人怀恨在心是完全合理的。

sentences.en: But Godwin does have all the patronage networks, all the connections, and it's presumably hard to do without him.
sentences.zh: 但戈德温确实拥有所有的赞助网络和人脉，没有他恐怕很难办成事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it requires both of them to play politics.
sentences.zh: 所以这需要他们两人都玩弄政治手段。

sentences.en: You know, it's a bit like, I suppose, Starmer bending the knee to Trump, even though he obviously hates him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这有点像斯塔默向特朗普屈膝，尽管他显然讨厌他。

sentences.en: You know, sometimes you have to do stuff to get on in geopolitics.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有时候为了在地缘政治中生存，你必须做些事情。

sentences.en: And this is kind of what's happening.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because they both have every reason for arriving at an accommodation because both depend on the other.
sentences.zh: 因为他们都有充分的理由达成妥协，因为双方都依赖对方。

sentences.en: So when Edward becomes king, Godwin is highly respectful.
sentences.zh: 所以当爱德华成为国王时，戈德温表现得非常恭敬。

sentences.en: He gives him an absolutely magnificent warship, which is all ornamented with gold.
sentences.zh: 他送给国王一艘极其壮观的战舰，上面装饰着黄金。

sentences.en: And it has a kind of crew of 80 warriors who are all wearing gilded armor.
sentences.zh: 船上有一支由80名身穿镀金盔甲的战士组成的船员队伍。

sentences.en: And in turn, Edward confirms Godwin in his rank as Earl of Wessex, which, of course, is what Godwin wants.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，爱德华确认了戈德温作为威塞克斯伯爵的地位，这当然是戈德温想要的。

sentences.en: And more than that, he promotes Godwin's sons.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他还提拔了戈德温的儿子们。

sentences.en: So Harold, for instance, even though he's only just 20 by this point, he becomes the Earl of East Anglia, which is a hugely powerful position.
sentences.zh: 比如哈罗德，尽管此时他刚满20岁，但他成为了东盎格鲁伯爵，这是一个权力巨大的职位。

sentences.en: And it means that Godwin and his sons are ruling a large swathe of England, albeit under the headship of Edward.
sentences.zh: 这意味着戈德温和他的儿子们统治着英格兰的一大片地区，尽管是在爱德华的领导下。

sentences.en: But there's a sense in which that's quite a nominal headship, because as you pointed out,
sentences.zh: 但某种程度上，那只是名义上的领导，因为正如你指出的，

sentences.en: Edward doesn't really have the contacts and the affinities that a king who had grown up in England would automatically have had.
sentences.zh: 爱德华并没有在英格兰长大的国王所自然拥有的那种人脉和亲缘关系。

sentences.en: He seems almost like a foreigner, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他看起来几乎像个外国人。

sentences.en: But obviously, the biggest symbol of this is who Edward marries, because when he arrives, he needs a wife.
sentences.zh: 但显然，这最大的象征是爱德华娶了谁，因为他到达时需要一位妻子。

sentences.en: And January 1043, he gets married.
sentences.zh: 1043年1月，他结婚了。

sentences.en: And three months later, his wife is crowned queen.
sentences.zh: 三个月后，他的妻子加冕为王后。

sentences.en: And the identity of this woman is Godwin's daughter, Edith.
sentences.zh: 而这个女人的身份就是戈德温的女儿，伊迪丝。

sentences.en: I mean, you could hardly have a more powerful, you know, physical, visual symbol of the reconciliation of the two men.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你很难找到比这更强大、更直观的两人和解的象征了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And for Godwin, it means that should Edith bear Edward's sons, then there's every chance that his grandson will be king of England.
sentences.zh: 对于戈德温来说，这意味着如果伊迪丝能为爱德华生下儿子，那么他的外孙很有可能成为英格兰国王。

sentences.en: So, I mean, it's an incredible prize.
sentences.zh: 所以，我是说，这是一个令人难以置信的奖赏。

sentences.en: Now, Edith herself is a very, very impressive woman.
sentences.zh: 现在，伊迪丝本人是一位非常、非常令人印象深刻的女性。

sentences.en: So I'm delighted to say that she was educated at Wilton, the great nunnery there.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴地说，她是在威尔顿受教育的，那里有一座伟大的修道院。

sentences.en: So she's not being, you know, she's not being ready to be a nun.
sentences.zh: 所以她并不是在准备当修女。

sentences.en: It's more like a kind of very expensive boarding school.
sentences.zh: 那更像是一种非常昂贵的寄宿学校。

sentences.en: She's very learned in music, in mathematics, in astronomy.
sentences.zh: 她在音乐、数学、天文学方面非常有学问。

sentences.en: She's supposed to have spoken five languages.
sentences.zh: 据说她会说五种语言。

sentences.en: So her native English, Danish, it got from her mother, Latin, French, and brilliantly Irish.
sentences.zh: 她的母语英语、从母亲那里继承的丹麦语、拉丁语、法语，还有令人惊叹的爱尔兰语。

sentences.en: She's very skilled at embroidery.
sentences.zh: 她非常擅长刺绣。

sentences.en: And she is described admittedly by this life of King Edward that she herself has sponsored as being ineffably beautiful.
sentences.zh: 爱德华国王的传记中确实提到，他亲自资助了这部传记，书中将她描述为美得无法言喻。

sentences.en: I'm sure she was.
sentences.zh: 我相信她确实如此。

sentences.en: So anyway, I was kind of reading the life of King Edward when we got our little kittens that would grow up to become Tostig and Edith.
sentences.zh: 总之，当我们领养那两只后来长成托斯蒂格和伊迪丝的小猫时，我正在读爱德华国王的传记。

sentences.en: And I called our girl cat, Edith, because I was reading about this.
sentences.zh: 我给我们的母猫取名伊迪丝，就是因为我当时在读这些内容。

sentences.en: So she's ineffably beautiful.
sentences.zh: 所以她美得无法言喻。

sentences.en: And there's this wonderful description of her.
sentences.zh: 书中对她有一段精彩的描述。

sentences.en: Edith, gem-like on the kingdom's breast, all virtues friend.
sentences.zh: “伊迪丝，王国胸前的宝石，一切美德之友。”

sentences.en: So that's how I like to think of my cat.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢这样看待我的猫。

sentences.en: But no Harold, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但没有哈罗德，汤姆。

sentences.en: No, so we did have a Harold as well, but he ran away.
sentences.zh: 不，我们确实也有一只叫哈罗德的猫，但它跑丢了。

sentences.en: Oh, crikey.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Really sad.
sentences.zh: 真令人难过。

sentences.en: So he got loSt.
sentences.zh: 它走丢了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So we just have Tostig and Edith.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在只有托斯蒂格和伊迪丝了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I think that it does Edith, my cat, great credit to have been named after this remarkable queen.
sentences.zh: 我觉得以这位非凡王后的名字来命名我的猫伊迪丝，是对它极大的赞誉。

sentences.en: She's very, very formidable.
sentences.zh: 她非常、非常令人敬畏。

sentences.en: And on royal charters, the moment that she has been crowned, she is appearing kind of second to Edward himself.
sentences.zh: 在皇家宪章上，她加冕的那一刻起，她的名字在某种程度上就排在爱德华本人之后。

sentences.en: And I guess for the people of England, her presence beside Edward on his throne is a kind of moving symbol of this reconciliation
sentences.zh: 我想对于英国人民来说，她陪伴在爱德华王座旁，是这种和解的一种动人象征，

sentences.en: between king and the great magnate who had put all England in his shadow, undertaken for the good of the English people
sentences.zh: 这种和解发生在国王与那位曾让整个英格兰笼罩在阴影下的权臣之间，这是为了英国人民的福祉而进行的，

sentences.en: and well befitting a Christian king with the care of his people uppermost in his mind.
sentences.zh: 也十分符合一位将子民福祉放在心上的基督教国王的身份。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But there is a cloud, right?
sentences.zh: 但还是有一片阴云，对吧？

sentences.en: There is one issue, which is there's one thing anybody who's ever heard of Henry VIII knows there is one thing a king has to do.
sentences.zh: 有一个问题，任何听说过亨利八世的人都知道，国王必须做的一件事就是传宗接代。

sentences.en: And Edward does not do it because they don't have any children.
sentences.zh: 而爱德华没有做到，因为他们没有孩子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the years go by, so four, five, six years, and still Edith hasn't given Edward an heir.
sentences.zh: 岁月流逝，四年、五年、六年过去了，伊迪丝依然没有为爱德华生下继承人。

sentences.en: It's harsh to blame it on Edith, Tom.
sentences.zh: 把责任归咎于伊迪丝是很苛刻的，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean...
sentences.zh: 我是说……

sentences.en: Well, it might be Edward's fault.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这可能是爱德华的问题。

sentences.en: It might be Edith's.
sentences.zh: 也可能是伊迪丝的问题。

sentences.en: The truth is that this is a marriage that has prompted enormous speculation.
sentences.zh: 事实是，这段婚姻引发了巨大的猜测。

sentences.en: And I guess that there are probably two principal theories as to why Edith does not give Edward a son.
sentences.zh: 我想关于伊迪丝为何没给爱德华生下儿子，大概有两个主要理论。

sentences.en: And the first of these, which is first mentioned by an English historian writing at Malmesbury called William, William of Malmesbury.
sentences.zh: 第一个理论最早由一位住在马姆斯伯里的英国历史学家威廉，即马姆斯伯里的威廉所提及。

sentences.en: I mean, he's very much, I think, like you in your children's book mode.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他很像你写童书时的样子。

sentences.en: He loves the story.
sentences.zh: 他热爱故事。

sentences.en: And, you know, if there's a kind of entertaining perspective to adopt, he will absolutely adopt it.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果有一个有趣的视角可以采用，他绝对会采用它。

sentences.en: Oh, thanks, Tom.
sentences.zh: 噢，谢谢你，汤姆。

sentences.en: That's kind.
sentences.zh: 你真好。

sentences.en: And he's very patriotic.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常爱国。

sentences.en: So the kind of, yeah, the Dominic Sandbrook of the 12th century.
sentences.zh: 所以他就像是12世纪的多米尼克·桑德布鲁克。

sentences.en: So William of Malmesbury's theory is that Edward is consumed with such hatred and resentment of Godwin that he can't bear to sleep with Godwin's daughter.
sentences.zh: 马姆斯伯里的威廉的理论是，爱德华对戈德温怀有极大的仇恨和怨恨，以至于他无法忍受与戈德温的女儿同床共枕。

sentences.en: That Edith may be ineffably beautiful and brilliant at speaking Irish and embroidery and stuff, but he doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 伊迪丝可能美得无法言喻，精通爱尔兰语、擅长刺绣等等，但他根本不在乎。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to have anything to do with her.
sentences.zh: 他不想和她有任何瓜葛。

sentences.en: Can't bear to be touched by her.
sentences.zh: 无法忍受她的触碰。

sentences.en: Don't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我不信。

sentences.en: I just don't believe that story.
sentences.zh: 我就是不相信那个故事。

sentences.en: I think if she's that beautiful, you'd overlook your animus against the father.
sentences.zh: 我想如果她那么美，你会忽略对她父亲的敌意。

sentences.en: In fact, the animus against the father might be an incentive.
sentences.zh: 事实上，对她父亲的敌意反而可能成为一种动力。

sentences.en: Well, possible support for this theory has been adduced in in the life of King Edward, where it says that Edward has consecrated himself to chastity.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在《爱德华国王传》中有人提出了支持这一理论的可能证据，书中说爱德华已立誓守贞。

sentences.en: OK, so maybe that's Edith's way of saying, well, you know, there were slight probleMs.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许那是伊迪丝委婉地说“嗯，你知道，确实存在一些小问题”的方式。

sentences.en: But I think there's another reason for that that will come to in due course.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这背后还有另一个原因，我们稍后会谈到。

sentences.en: And I would also just throw in here the opinion of Pauline Stafford, who is the great expert on 11th century English queens.
sentences.zh: 我还要顺便提一下宝琳·斯塔福德的观点，她是11世纪英国王后研究方面的权威专家。

sentences.en: And she says it is futile to speculate on the sex lives, sex drives or sexuality of 11th century kings from such sparse and partial evidence.
sentences.zh: 她说，仅凭如此稀少且片面的证据去推测11世纪国王的性生活、性冲动或性取向是徒劳的。

sentences.en: Tom, if we if we adopted that that attitude, I mean, our podcast would be about 20 minutes shorter.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，如果我们采取那种态度，我们的播客大概会缩短20分钟。

sentences.en: I'm not sure that's true.
sentences.zh: 我不确定那是真的。

sentences.en: I think I think we've repeatedly said that we can't impose kind of 21st century standards of sexual psychology.
sentences.zh: 我想我们已经反复说过，我们不能强加21世纪的性心理标准。

sentences.en: We have.
sentences.zh: 我们说过。

sentences.en: We try not to.
sentences.zh: 我们尽量不那样做。

sentences.en: We normally say that after we've spent the previous eight minutes.
sentences.zh: 我们通常是在花了前八分钟进行猜测之后才这么说的。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: Entertainingly speculating, which is what we've just done.
sentences.zh: 进行有趣的猜测，这正是我们刚才所做的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: But I don't think that that is the key to it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为那并不是问题的关键。

sentences.en: So the other possibility, of course, is that Edith or Edward can't have children.
sentences.zh: 所以另一种可能性当然是，伊迪丝或爱德华无法生育。

sentences.en: That seems to me a much more plausible explanation.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是一种更合理的解释。

sentences.en: I mean, Edward would want to father children.
sentences.zh: 我是说，爱德华会想要生儿育女的。

sentences.en: He would want to propagate his line.
sentences.zh: 他会想要延续他的血脉。

sentences.en: And I think the evidence for this is that by the end of 1050.
sentences.zh: 我认为这方面的证据是，到1050年底时。

sentences.en: So that's, you know, five years after his marriage to Edith.
sentences.zh: 也就是他与伊迪丝结婚五年后。

sentences.en: It's clear that he is manoeuvring to divorce her and by implication, remarry.
sentences.zh: 很明显，他正在策划与她离婚，并暗示要再婚。

sentences.en: And I think the consequence of this is the first great crisis in English history precipitated by a king's desire to get a new wife.
sentences.zh: 我认为其后果是英国历史上第一次因国王想要娶新妻子而引发的重大危机。

sentences.en: So you alluded to Henry VIII.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到了亨利八世。

sentences.en: This is, you know, this is where that trend all kicks off.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是那个趋势的开端。

sentences.en: So to pursue that thread, the issue for Henry VIII, of course, was that he was setting himself against the king of Spain, the pope and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 顺着这条线索说，亨利八世的问题当然在于他是在与西班牙国王、教皇等人作对。

sentences.en: The issue for Edward is that he is setting himself against, in the short term, a more dangerous opponent, because that, of course, is Godwin,
sentences.zh: 爱德华的问题在于，他在短期内是在与一个更危险的对手作对，因为那个人当然是戈德温，

sentences.en: the most powerful person in the kingdom.
sentences.zh: 王国中最有权势的人。

sentences.en: So, well, he doesn't he does have allies, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他确实有盟友，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that's one thing we should say, because there are other magnates who don't like Godwin.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是我们应该指出的，因为还有其他不喜欢戈德温的权贵。

sentences.en: Yeah, so there are two in particular.
sentences.zh: 是的，特别是两位。

sentences.en: There's the Earl of Northumberland, which by this point is a Dane called Seward.
sentences.zh: 一位是诺森伯兰伯爵，当时是一位名叫西瓦德的丹麦人。

sentences.en: And people who've read or watched Macbeth may remember that he features in that.
sentences.zh: 读过或看过《麦克白》的人可能记得他在其中出现过。

sentences.en: Historically, Seward launches two invasions of Scotland against Macbeth.
sentences.zh: 历史上，西瓦德曾两次发动对苏格兰的入侵以对抗麦克白。

sentences.en: And Edward really trusts him.
sentences.zh: 爱德华非常信任他。

sentences.en: The other is a guy called Leofric.
sentences.zh: 另一位叫利奥弗里克。

sentences.en: And he is the Earl of Mercia.
sentences.zh: 他是麦西亚伯爵。

sentences.en: And he, again, is one of the kind of English nobles who has profited from the Danish invasion.
sentences.zh: 他也是从丹麦入侵中获利的英国贵族之一。

sentences.en: It's possible that Alfgifu, who is Canute's first wife, the mother of Harold Harefoot, that she may have been related to him.
sentences.zh: 阿尔夫吉夫，也就是克努特的第一任妻子、哈罗德·哈雷福特的母亲，可能与他有亲戚关系。

sentences.en: Well, that would make sense because he'd backed Harefoot, hadn't he, in the succession crisis?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这说得通，因为他在继承危机中支持了哈雷福特，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is why Leofric is where he is as Earl of Mercia.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是利奥弗里克为何能担任麦西亚伯爵的原因。

sentences.en: And he is probably best known in English folklore as the husband of a woman called Gogifu, which comes to be Godiva, as in Lady Godiva,
sentences.zh: 他在英国民间传说中最出名的身份可能是一位名叫戈吉夫的女性的丈夫，后来演变成了戈黛娃夫人，也就是戈黛娃夫人，

sentences.en: who rides naked through the streets of Coventry.
sentences.zh: 她曾裸体骑马穿过考文垂的街道。

sentences.en: Yeah, best thing that's ever happened in Coventry.
sentences.zh: 没错，这是考文垂发生过的最好的事。

sentences.en: And it's interesting because Leofric in that is cast as a man who is exacting too many taxes.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，利奥弗里克在那个故事中被塑造成一个征收过多税款的人。

sentences.en: And it's a reminder again of the fact that in the 11th century, the English are the most heavily taxed people in Western Europe.
sentences.zh: 这再次提醒我们，在11世纪，英国人是西欧赋税最沉重的人民。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it's all about the ability of earls to extract money from people.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都关乎伯爵们从人民身上榨取钱财的能力。

sentences.en: And then what about the Normans?
sentences.zh: 那么诺曼人呢？

sentences.en: Because Edward, of course, has spent so many years in Normandy and he brings some Normans with him when he comes, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为爱德华当然在诺曼底度过了很多年，他来的时候带了一些诺曼人，不是吗？

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他确实带了。

sentences.en: Yes, he does.
sentences.zh: 是的，他带了。

sentences.en: And we talked yesterday about how in France there is this brewing military revolution of which the most prominent symbol is the castle.
sentences.zh: 我们昨天谈到法国正在酝酿一场军事革命，其最显著的象征就是城堡。

sentences.en: And actually, there are Normans who are given lands in England and who build castles.
sentences.zh: 事实上，确实有一些诺曼人在英国被授予土地并建造了城堡。

sentences.en: So one of them is a brother-in-law of Edward.
sentences.zh: 其中一位是爱德华的姐夫。

sentences.en: He's called Ralph and he has the brilliant supriché of the timid, which I think is what I would have if I was a Norman lord.
sentences.zh: 他叫拉尔夫，有一个绝妙的绰号叫“胆怯者”，我想如果我是诺曼领主，我也会有这个绰号。

sentences.en: And he becomes the Earl of Herefordshire and he builds a castle there.
sentences.zh: 他成为了赫里福德伯爵，并在那里建造了一座城堡。

sentences.en: There is also an abbot from a place called Jumiege.
sentences.zh: 还有一位来自朱米耶日地方的修道院院长。

sentences.en: He's called Robert.
sentences.zh: 他叫罗伯特。

sentences.en: And he is appointed by Edward, Bishop of London.
sentences.zh: 他被爱德华任命为伦敦主教。

sentences.en: And then in 1051, Archbishop of Canterbury.
sentences.zh: 随后在1051年，又被任命为坎特伯雷大主教。

sentences.en: So to some degree, the Norman, people always say, what if the Norman conquest never happened?
sentences.zh: 所以某种程度上，人们总是问，如果诺曼征服从未发生会怎样？

sentences.en: But the integration of the English and the Norman worlds has already started long before 1066.
sentences.zh: 但英格兰和诺曼世界的融合早在1066年之前就开始了。

sentences.en: Well, it goes all the way back to Emma marrying Æthelred.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这可以追溯到艾玛嫁给埃塞尔雷德的时候。

sentences.en: I mean, it's been an ongoing process, but Godwin certainly doesn't like it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是一个持续的过程，但戈德温显然不喜欢它。

sentences.en: And particularly the appointment of Robert of Jumiege as Archbishop of Canterbury.
sentences.zh: 特别是任命罗伯特·德·朱米耶日为坎特伯雷大主教。

sentences.en: He's furious about this because he'd wanted one of his own placemen to get the job.
sentences.zh: 他对此感到愤怒，因为他本想让自己的亲信得到这个职位。

sentences.en: And it precipitates a rapid meltdown in relations between Edward and Godwin.
sentences.zh: 这导致了爱德华和戈德温之间关系的迅速破裂。

sentences.en: And I think the pace of the meltdown is reflective of the fact that Edward is starting to angle now to try and get rid of Edith.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种破裂的速度反映了爱德华现在开始试图摆脱伊迪丝的事实。

sentences.en: Because he wants children.
sentences.zh: 因为他想要孩子。

sentences.en: But it's certainly not helped by the new Archbishop of Canterbury, who is openly and repeatedly snubbing Godwin.
sentences.zh: 但新任坎特伯雷大主教公开且反复地冷落戈德温，这无疑让情况雪上加霜。

sentences.en: And also lots of the Normans who have come over to London or, you know, maybe heading back to Normandy or whatever, are disrespecting Godwin quite seriously.
sentences.zh: 而且许多来到伦敦的诺曼人，或者说可能正准备回诺曼底的人，都在严重地不尊重戈德温。

sentences.en: Almost as though they're being prompted to, perhaps, by the king.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像是受到国王的暗示一样。

sentences.en: I mean, we don't know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们不知道。

sentences.en: That might be a conspiracy through too far.
sentences.zh: 那可能有点过度阴谋论了。

sentences.en: But there's a notorious occasion in August 1051 where there's a massive fracas in Dover when a Norman nobleman in his retinue are supposedly attacked.
sentences.zh: 但在1051年8月发生了一件臭名昭著的事，多佛发生了一场大规模骚乱，当时一位诺曼贵族及其随从据称遭到了袭击。

sentences.en: And Edward is furious about this.
sentences.zh: 爱德华对此大发雷霆。

sentences.en: And he orders Godwin to go and ravage Dover as a punishment.
sentences.zh: 他命令戈德温去蹂躏多佛作为惩罚。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, this is a traditional form of English justice.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是英国传统的司法形式。

sentences.en: We talked about how Edgar was always ravaging places that annoyed him.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到过埃德加总是蹂躏那些惹恼他的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Hence his nickname, the Peaceable.
sentences.zh: 所以他才有“和平者”这个绰号。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And Godwin refuses.
sentences.zh: 而戈德温拒绝了。

sentences.en: These are his people.
sentences.zh: 这些人是他的子民。

sentences.en: He is the Earl of, essentially, of Southern England.
sentences.zh: 他本质上是英格兰南部的伯爵。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to have to do that.
sentences.zh: 他不想那样做。

sentences.en: He's put in a completely invidious position.
sentences.zh: 他被置于一个极其尴尬的境地。

sentences.en: And you can't help thinking that it's a deliberate manoeuvre on the part of Edward's to force Godwin into a corner.
sentences.zh: 你不得不认为这是爱德华为了将戈德温逼入绝境而采取的蓄意策略。

sentences.en: And the consequence of this is that by September 1051, Godwin and his sons are starting to raise their levies.
sentences.zh: 其后果是，到1051年9月，戈德温和他的儿子们开始召集他们的征召兵。

sentences.en: They're preparing for war.
sentences.zh: 他们正在为战争做准备。

sentences.en: And Edward then summons Seward and Leofric, the earls of Northumberland and Mercia, to raise their levies and come to his defence.
sentences.zh: 爱德华随后召集诺森伯兰和麦西亚的伯爵西瓦德和利奥弗里克，召集他们的征召兵前来护驾。

sentences.en: And these two great armies confront each other.
sentences.zh: 这两支大军对峙起来。

sentences.en: You know, they're lined up, but then they hesitate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们排好了阵势，但随后犹豫了。

sentences.en: And the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle explains why.
sentences.zh: 《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》解释了原因。

sentences.en: Some of them considered that it would be great folly if they joined battle.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人认为，如果开战将是极大的愚蠢。

sentences.en: Almost all the noblest in England were present in those two companies.
sentences.zh: 英格兰几乎所有最显赫的人都在那两支队伍中。

sentences.en: And they were convinced that they would be leaving the country open to the invasion of our enemies and be bringing utter ruin upon themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们深信，如果不这样做，国家就会门户大开，任由敌人入侵，最终导致他们自己彻底毁灭。

sentences.en: Isn't that interesting that they're already anticipating the possibility that, you know, neighbouring predators might make a move?
sentences.zh: 他们已经预料到，你知道，邻近的掠夺者可能会采取行动，这难道不耐人寻味吗？

sentences.en: But, I mean, think about it.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，仔细想想。

sentences.en: These are all people who've lived through the Danish conqueSt.
sentences.zh: 这些人都是经历过丹麦征服的人。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm sure they're thinking of the Vikings rather than the Normans.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我相信他们想到的是维京人，而不是诺曼人。

sentences.en: But, I mean, you know, they know that a house divided is, I mean, it's not a good place to be.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，你知道，他们知道一个分裂的家庭，我的意思是，那可不是什么好地方。

sentences.en: So negotiations are opened and it's agreed that Godwin will come to London in a fortnight's time after this meeting and he will be put in trial.
sentences.zh: 于是双方开启了谈判，并达成协议：戈德温将在这次会议两周后前往伦敦接受审判。

sentences.en: And Godwin agrees and he's planning to go to London with his army.
sentences.zh: 戈德温同意了，并计划带着他的军队前往伦敦。

sentences.en: But his levies start to melt away.
sentences.zh: 但他的征召兵开始纷纷逃离。

sentences.en: And even before the two weeks are up, he realises that, you know, he's finished.
sentences.zh: 甚至在两周期限还没到之前，他就意识到，你知道，他完了。

sentences.en: And so he takes horse, takes ship, heads off to Flanders.
sentences.zh: 于是他骑上马，乘上船，前往佛兰德斯。

sentences.en: And his wife and sons also flee.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子和儿子们也随之逃亡。

sentences.en: So Harold flees to Ireland.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德则逃往了爱尔兰。

sentences.en: The only significant figure of the Godwin family who is left is Edith, Edward's queen.
sentences.zh: 戈德温家族唯一留下的重要人物是伊迪丝，也就是爱德华的王后。

sentences.en: And she is immediately packed off to a nunnery.
sentences.zh: 她随即被送往了一座修道院。

sentences.en: Edith will say that it was Wilton and will imply that it was a kind of a rather pleasant retirement.
sentences.zh: 伊迪丝会说那是威尔顿修道院，并暗示那是一种相当惬意的退休生活。

sentences.en: But probably she is sent off to another nunnery, which effectively serves as a prison.
sentences.zh: 但她很可能被送往了另一座修道院，那里实际上就是一座监狱。

sentences.en: So shades of the Merovingians, which we talked about in the Franks.
sentences.zh: 这让人想起了我们在法兰克人那一章里谈到的墨洛温王朝的影子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So here we are in the end of 1051.
sentences.zh: 所以现在时间来到了1051年底。

sentences.en: The Godwins, it looks like they're out, they're down.
sentences.zh: 戈德温家族看起来已经出局了，他们倒台了。

sentences.en: But I guess the issue for Edward now is that by kicking out the Godwins, he has thrown his lot in completely with Seward and Leofric.
sentences.zh: 但我认为爱德华现在的问题是，通过驱逐戈德温家族，他已经完全与西瓦德和利奥弗里克站在了一起。

sentences.en: And he's in their power to some extent, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他在某种程度上受制于他们，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, basically because there is now no counterbalance to them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上是因为现在没有任何力量能与他们抗衡了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so it's not surprising that they are confirmed in more grants of land.
sentences.zh: 所以他们获得更多的土地赏赐也就不足为奇了。

sentences.en: Harold has been the Earl of East Anglia.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德曾是东盎格利亚伯爵。

sentences.en: There's now a vacancy.
sentences.zh: 现在那里空缺了。

sentences.en: So Leofric's son, Alfgar, he gets that job.
sentences.zh: 于是利奥弗里克的儿子阿尔夫加得到了这个职位。

sentences.en: So clearly, you know, jobs for the boys.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，你知道，这就是所谓的“任人唯亲”。

sentences.en: I mean, that's part of the deal.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是交易的一部分。

sentences.en: But Edward does have other allies beyond England, because, of course, he has all these contacts in Normandy.
sentences.zh: 但爱德华在英格兰之外确实还有其他盟友，因为他当然在诺曼底有各种人脉。

sentences.en: And it is now in the wake of Godwin's flight that the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle reports a key development.
sentences.zh: 正是在戈德温逃亡之后，《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》记载了一个关键进展。

sentences.en: And it's a sentence that has been, you know, so discussed.
sentences.zh: 这是一个被，你知道，讨论得非常多的句子。

sentences.en: And I'll read it.
sentences.zh: 我来读一下。

sentences.en: Then came Duke William from beyond the sea with a great retinue of Frenchmen.
sentences.zh: “随后，威廉公爵带着一大批法国随从从海外而来。”

sentences.en: And the king received him and as many of his companions as it pleased him.
sentences.zh: “国王接待了他，以及随他前来的随从，人数随国王心意。”

sentences.en: So what does receive mean?
sentences.zh: 那么“接待”是什么意思呢？

sentences.en: I think it means slightly more than just, you know, oh, come in and have a drink.
sentences.zh: 我认为它的含义比单纯的“哦，进来喝杯酒吧”要深远得多。

sentences.en: No, it's more kind of William is almost becoming his vassal.
sentences.zh: 不，这更像是威廉几乎要成为他的附庸了。

sentences.en: He's offering him kind of pledges of support in a way that affirms Edward's rank as king.
sentences.zh: 他以某种方式向他承诺支持，从而肯定了爱德华作为国王的地位。

sentences.en: But the question then is, well, what has Edward given William in return?
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，爱德华又给了威廉什么作为回报呢？

sentences.en: And the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle doesn't say.
sentences.zh: 《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》没有说。

sentences.en: No English source says.
sentences.zh: 没有任何英国史料提到过。

sentences.en: Yes, but Norman sources insist that what Edward has done is to promise William the crown, should Edward not have sons.
sentences.zh: 是的，但诺曼史料坚称，爱德华所做的是承诺如果他没有儿子，就将王位传给威廉。

sentences.en: So in the words of David Douglas, who's the author of the definitive recent biography of William,
sentences.zh: 用大卫·道格拉斯的话来说，他是威廉近期权威传记的作者，

sentences.en: there can be no reasonable doubt that before the end of 1051, he had nominated William of Normandy as his heir.
sentences.zh: “毫无疑问，在1051年底之前，他已经提名诺曼底的威廉为他的继承人。”

sentences.en: But some historians do doubt it, though, don't they?
sentences.zh: 但有些历史学家确实对此表示怀疑，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, some historians are like, well, we cannot be certain what the arrangement was.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些历史学家会说，我们无法确定当时的安排究竟是什么。

sentences.en: And it may have been much less, you know, he may have made noises, but not been definitive.
sentences.zh: 而且可能远没有那么正式，你知道，他可能只是随口提过，但并没有定论。

sentences.en: I mean, the fact that it's so vague in the sources.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，史料中对此描述得如此模糊，本身就说明了问题。

sentences.en: Well, I think that that Edward, for as long as he is childless, uses the possibility that he could nominate someone as king as a kind of bargaining chip.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为爱德华只要还没有子嗣，就会利用“他可以提名某人为国王”的可能性作为一种谈判筹码。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In a way, it's it's almost the strongest card he has to play.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这几乎是他手中最强的一张牌。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I'm fairly sure he does suggest this to William.
sentences.zh: 而且我相当肯定他确实向威廉暗示过这一点。

sentences.en: But, of course, one of the reasons why he does it is that he is kind of.
sentences.zh: 但当然，他这么做的一个原因是，他有点……

sentences.en: You know, he's looking to get a new wife.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他想再娶一个妻子。

sentences.en: He's looking to have a son.
sentences.zh: 他想生个儿子。

sentences.en: And if he has a son, then, you know, no problem.
sentences.zh: 如果他有了儿子，那么，你知道，就没问题了。

sentences.en: William won't become king.
sentences.zh: 威廉就不会成为国王。

sentences.en: But the problem is, of course, that, you know, he doesn't yet have a wife or a son in place.
sentences.zh: 但问题当然是，你知道，他还没有合适的妻子或儿子。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The succession had gone through.
sentences.zh: 如果继承程序已经走完。

sentences.en: You could imagine quite a kind of, you know, a peaceable process of of succession that William might might well have become king.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一个相当，你知道，和平的继承过程，威廉很可能真的会成为国王。

sentences.en: And it would have the whole process would have been a lot less brutal.
sentences.zh: 整个过程会比后来残酷得多。

sentences.en: But the thing is that all of this is dependent on Godwin and his family remaining safely in exile.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，这一切都取决于戈德温及其家族能否安全地流亡在外。

sentences.en: And I guess that if there is a theme of this series, it's the fact that people who are driven into exile always come back.
sentences.zh: 我想如果这个系列有一个主题的话，那就是：被流放的人总是会回来的。

sentences.en: They always come back.
sentences.zh: 他们总是会回来。

sentences.en: Well, they I mean, all of the people, almost all the people we talk about spend time in exile, don't they?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们……我的意思是，我们谈到的几乎所有人都在流亡中度过了一段时间，不是吗？

sentences.en: And make astonishing comebacks.
sentences.zh: 并且上演了惊人的回归。

sentences.en: Astonishing comebacks.
sentences.zh: 惊人的回归。

sentences.en: And this is what happens in August 1052.
sentences.zh: 这就是1052年8月发生的事情。

sentences.en: So the year after Godwin's flight, Godwin has not been twiddling his thumbs.
sentences.zh: 在戈德温逃亡一年后，戈德温并没有闲着。

sentences.en: He has been recruiting an enormous fleet.
sentences.zh: 他一直在招募一支庞大的舰队。

sentences.en: He's been raising an army and in the summer of 1052, he sails from Flanders with his fleet.
sentences.zh: 他一直在集结军队，1052年夏天，他带着舰队从佛兰德斯起航。

sentences.en: Harold, meanwhile, has been raising a fleet in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，哈罗德一直在爱尔兰集结舰队。

sentences.en: The two of them meet on the south coast of England and they start kind of ravaging the south coaSt.
sentences.zh: 两人在英格兰南海岸会合，开始蹂躏南海岸。

sentences.en: And Edward is thrown into a panic.
sentences.zh: 爱德华陷入了恐慌。

sentences.en: He doesn't have the levies to hand or indeed the fleet because he's actually cut back on the taxes that would have kept the fleet going.
sentences.zh: 他手头没有征召兵，也没有舰队，因为他实际上削减了维持舰队所需的税收。

sentences.en: Very, very foolish move.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常愚蠢的举动。

sentences.en: And so he's he's a bit stuck.
sentences.zh: 所以他有点陷入困境了。

sentences.en: And 14th of September, the Godwins sail up the Thames in triumph and they dock at the south end of London Bridge.
sentences.zh: 9月14日，戈德温家族乘船沿泰晤士河凯旋而上，停靠在伦敦桥南端。

sentences.en: So in Southwark, London is held against them.
sentences.zh: 在南华克，伦敦城正严阵以待对抗他们。

sentences.en: It's got the great Roman walls.
sentences.zh: 那里有宏伟的罗马城墙。

sentences.en: And Edward thinks, well, I can defy them.
sentences.zh: 爱德华心想，好吧，我可以反抗他们。

sentences.en: But the mass of people, not just in London, but across England, you know, they they say it's not worth fighting over.
sentences.zh: 但广大民众，不仅是在伦敦，在整个英格兰，你知道，他们说这不值得为此打仗。

sentences.en: And also there's quite a lot of resentment of the rumours that Edward has nominated William of Normandy, his heir.
sentences.zh: 而且人们对爱德华提名诺曼底的威廉为继承人的传言也颇有怨言。

sentences.en: People don't like the Normans.
sentences.zh: 人们不喜欢诺曼人。

sentences.en: They think I would rather have Godwin than a load of foreigners.
sentences.zh: 他们心想：我宁愿要戈德温，也不要一堆外国人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so Edward ultimately finds himself with no choice but to welcome the Godwins back.
sentences.zh: 所以爱德华最终发现自己别无选择，只能欢迎戈德温家族回来。

sentences.en: And Godwin plays it very cool.
sentences.zh: 而戈德温表现得非常冷静。

sentences.en: You know, he doesn't humiliate the king.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他没有羞辱国王。

sentences.en: He kneels before him.
sentences.zh: 他在国王面前下跪。

sentences.en: He begs his royal forgiveness.
sentences.zh: 他恳求国王的宽恕。

sentences.en: He insists that he'd been misrepresented and is innocent of all the charges against him.
sentences.zh: 他坚称自己被诬陷了，对所有针对他的指控都是清白的。

sentences.en: And Edward has no choice but to accept this.
sentences.zh: 爱德华别无选择，只能接受。

sentences.en: And both Godwin and Harold are restored to their respective earldoMs.
sentences.zh: 戈德温和哈罗德都恢复了各自的伯爵领地。

sentences.en: And Edith returns in triumph from her exile and imprisonment in her nunnery.
sentences.zh: 伊迪丝也从流亡和修道院监禁中凯旋归来。

sentences.en: Back to her husband's side.
sentences.zh: 回到了丈夫身边。

sentences.en: There she is, an anointed queen by the side of her husband, the anointed king.
sentences.zh: 她就在那里，作为受膏王后，站在她丈夫——那位受膏国王的身边。

sentences.en: And clearly this means that there is now no more talk of divorce, which in turn probably means that there is no more prospect of Edward having an heir.
sentences.zh: 这显然意味着再也没有人谈论离婚了，这反过来可能意味着爱德华再也不可能有继承人了。

sentences.en: And the life of King Edward, I mean, it celebrates this in delighted tones.
sentences.zh: 而《爱德华国王传》对此进行了欣喜若狂的赞美。

sentences.en: The whole country settled down in peaceful tranquility.

sentences.en: Beyond the walls of London, beside the River Thames, there stood a monastery dedicated to St. Peter.
sentences.zh: 在伦敦城墙外，泰晤士河畔，矗立着一座献给圣彼得的修道院。

sentences.en: It was an insignificant place, and under its abbot, only a small community of monks served ChriSt.
sentences.zh: 那是一个不起眼的地方，在院长领导下，只有一小群僧侣在此侍奉基督。

sentences.en: The king, therefore, devoted as he was to God, fixed his attention on the spot.
sentences.zh: 因此，虔诚的国王将目光投向了这里。

sentences.en: For not only was it close to a rich and famous city, but it was also a delightful spot, surrounded with fertile land and green fields, and near the main channel of the river,
sentences.zh: 因为它不仅靠近一座富饶而著名的城市，而且是一个令人愉悦的地方，四周环绕着肥沃的土地和绿色的田野，靠近河流的主航道，

sentences.en: which bore abundant merchandise of wares of every kind for sale from the whole world to the town on its banks.
sentences.zh: 河道运载着来自世界各地、供岸边城镇出售的各种丰富商品。

sentences.en: So, that's an account in the life of King Edward, about how Edward the Confessor came to build a great abbey, or a minster, as the Anglo-Saxons called it, to the west of London.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是《爱德华国王传》中关于忏悔者爱德华如何在伦敦以西建造一座大修道院（盎格鲁-撒克逊人称之为“明斯特”）的记载。

sentences.en: So, it's to the west of London, and it's a minster, and guess what they end up calling it?
sentences.zh: 所以，它在伦敦西边，是一座“明斯特”，你猜他们最后叫它什么？

sentences.en: Westminster!
sentences.zh: 威斯敏斯特！

sentences.en: Duh!
sentences.zh: 废话！

sentences.en: Well, amazing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，太神奇了。

sentences.en: So, Tom, this is the origin of Westminster Abbey.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，这就是威斯敏斯特教堂的起源。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And as you said, it comes from the life of King Edward, which, remember, is commissioned by Edith, his queen, and so her fingerprints are all over this account.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，它源于爱德华国王的一生，请记住，这是由他的王后伊迪丝委托撰写的，所以这份记载里到处都是她的影子。

sentences.en: And this life has two particular goals.
sentences.zh: 而这本传记有两个特别的目标。

sentences.en: And the first is to cast Edward as essentially a saintly figure, a confessor.
sentences.zh: 第一个是把爱德华塑造成一个本质上圣洁的人物，一位忏悔者。

sentences.en: And the second is to associate herself, Edith, with this saintliness.
sentences.zh: 第二个是把她自己，也就是伊迪丝，与这种圣洁联系起来。

sentences.en: And this is why, after this life has described how Edward sponsors the building of his great abbey at Westminster,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在这本传记描述了爱德华如何资助他在威斯敏斯特建造宏伟的教堂之后，

sentences.en: it then goes on to describe how Edith rebuilt Wilton, you know, where she'd been raised, and this kind of great centre of Wessax and holiness, to rebuild this abbey in stone.
sentences.zh: 它接着描述了伊迪丝如何重建威尔顿——你知道的，那是她成长的地方，也是威塞克斯和神圣的伟大中心——将这座修道院重建为石质建筑。

sentences.en: And that is kind of essentially casting her as her husband's partner in godliness.
sentences.zh: 这本质上是将她塑造成她丈夫在敬虔事业上的伙伴。

sentences.en: And what the life does not do when it accounts Edward's building of Westminster Abbey is to point out that he's also building an enormous palace.
sentences.zh: 当这本传记叙述爱德华建造威斯敏斯特教堂时，它没有提到的是，他同时还在建造一座巨大的宫殿。

sentences.en: So, pretty much where the Houses of Parliament are now.
sentences.zh: 就在现在议会大厦所在地附近。

sentences.en: So, essentially, it's an enormous royal complex.
sentences.zh: 所以，本质上，这是一个巨大的皇家建筑群。

sentences.en: But she doesn't want that mentioned, because it slightly detracts from the sense of him as a man utterly devoted to God.
sentences.zh: 但她不想提及这一点，因为这会稍微削弱他作为一个全心全意侍奉上帝的人的形象。

sentences.en: And likewise, it's this life, which we said before, which insists that Edward willingly consecrates himself to virginity.
sentences.zh: 同样，正如我们之前所说，正是这本传记坚持认为爱德华自愿发誓守贞。

sentences.en: And I think that we can see reasons for that that have nothing to do with Edward supposedly not allowing Edith into his bed.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们可以看出其中的原因，这与爱德华据称不让伊迪丝同床没有任何关系。

sentences.en: Because, essentially, by saying that Edward has consecrated himself to chastity,
sentences.zh: 因为，本质上，通过宣称爱德华发誓守贞，

sentences.en: it's veiling the failure of Edith to give him a child, which is the prime responsibility of a queen.
sentences.zh: 这掩盖了伊迪丝未能为他生下子嗣的事实，而这正是王后的首要职责。

sentences.en: And it doesn't matter how unfair that is.
sentences.zh: 而且这公不公平并不重要。

sentences.en: If you don't, essentially, you've failed as a queen.
sentences.zh: 如果你做不到，本质上，你就没能尽到王后的职责。

sentences.en: And also, it associates her with this kind of saintly project of chastity, because, by extension, she is a virgin as a result.
sentences.zh: 而且，这也将她与这种圣洁的守贞计划联系在一起，因为推而广之，她也因此保持了贞洁。

sentences.en: And not only that, but because if she paints Edward as this sort of, you know, he's thinking about God and his mind is on higher things and all of that.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，因为如果她把爱德华描绘成那种，你知道的，他一心只想着上帝，思想专注于更高尚的事物等等。

sentences.en: I mean, people, yeah, they're like, oh, brilliant.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们，是的，他们会觉得，哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: But it sort of emphasises that her family, Godwin and his sons, have been the people who've actually been making the machine work and keeping England going.
sentences.zh: 但这在某种程度上强调了她的家族，戈德温和他的儿子们，才是真正让国家机器运转并维持英国运作的人。

sentences.en: And so it makes them look good, too.
sentences.zh: 所以这也让他们看起来很不错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, the life, even as it's celebrating Edward as this kind of otherworldly figure who spends his whole time hanging out with monks,
sentences.zh: 所以，这本传记，即使在歌颂爱德华是一个整天与僧侣为伍的超凡脱俗的人物时，

sentences.en: it's emphasising how Harold and Tostig are, you know, and all his other brothers, he's got hundreds of brothers, how they are setting their shoulder to the wheel
sentences.zh: 它也在强调哈罗德和托斯蒂格，你知道的，还有他所有的其他兄弟——他有几百个兄弟——他们是如何齐心协力，

sentences.en: and labouring hard in the cause of England.
sentences.zh: 并为英国的事业辛勤工作。

sentences.en: And in fact, it's clear, even from the life of King Edward, that he's not spending his whole time with monks.
sentences.zh: 事实上，即使从《爱德华国王传》中也可以清楚地看出，他并没有把所有时间都花在僧侣身上。

sentences.en: Even the life has to admit that actually he's spending most of his time hunting.
sentences.zh: 即使是这本传记也不得不承认，实际上他大部分时间都在打猎。

sentences.en: It's clear that Edward essentially has been sidelined, that he's become a bit of a cipher.
sentences.zh: 很明显，爱德华本质上已经被边缘化了，他已经变成了一个无足轻重的人。

sentences.en: But he's really not spending his whole time confessing.
sentences.zh: 但他真的没有把所有时间都花在忏悔上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's killing a lot of deer.
sentences.zh: 他杀了很多鹿。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And I think this sense of Edward that the life is promoting as a man almost kind of too good for the world is heightened by a dramatic development in 1053.
sentences.zh: 我认为这本传记所宣扬的爱德华那种几乎对这个世界来说太好的人的形象，在1053年的一个戏剧性事件中得到了加强。

sentences.en: And if people going into exile and coming back is one theme of this series, then another is people at meals unexpectedly dying of choking fits.
sentences.zh: 如果说人们流亡又回来是本系列的一个主题，那么另一个主题就是人们在用餐时意外死于窒息。

sentences.en: So this happens at Easter in 1053.
sentences.zh: 这发生在1053年的复活节。

sentences.en: Godwin is with the King in Winchester at a great Easter feaSt.
sentences.zh: 戈德温与国王在温彻斯特参加盛大的复活节宴会。

sentences.en: And he chokes to death.
sentences.zh: 然后他窒息而死。

sentences.en: But there's no suspicion here of foul play, is there?
sentences.zh: 但这里并没有关于谋杀的怀疑，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, this just seems like an occupational hazard of, are they just eating an enormous amount of ill-cooked meat?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来就像是一种职业风险，他们是不是只是吃了太多烹饪不当的肉？

sentences.en: Very tough meat.
sentences.zh: 非常硬的肉。

sentences.en: I mean, who knows?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I don't think there's any hint.
sentences.zh: 我不认为有任何暗示。

sentences.en: And it doesn't really alter Edward's position because he has no choice but to appoint Harold as Earl of Wessex.
sentences.zh: 而且这并没有真正改变爱德华的地位，因为他别无选择，只能任命哈罗德为威塞克斯伯爵。

sentences.en: That's the moment where we began this series.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们开始这个系列的那一刻。

sentences.en: And I think actually it kind of makes him look even weaker because there's a sense of a generational shift.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这实际上让他看起来更软弱了，因为有一种代际更替的感觉。

sentences.en: You know, this new generation of Earls, Harold and so on, are stepping up to the plate.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这新一代的伯爵，哈罗德等等，正在挺身而出。

sentences.en: And Edward looks kind of elderly and decrepit and a bit out of the loop.
sentences.zh: 而爱德华看起来有点老态龙钟，有点脱离了核心圈子。

sentences.en: But there is a bit of a balance of power thing going on here, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 但这其中确实存在一种权力平衡，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because Harold had been Earl of East Anglia, but now he's taken over the kind of premier job, which is Earl of Wessex.
sentences.zh: 因为哈罗德曾是东盎格利亚伯爵，但现在他接手了最重要的职位，即威塞克斯伯爵。

sentences.en: So he's got the heartland region.
sentences.zh: 所以他拥有了核心区域。

sentences.en: But he's replaced in East Anglia by a guy called Elfgar, who is the son of Leofric.
sentences.zh: 但他被一个叫埃尔夫加的人取代了，他是利奥弗里克的儿子。

sentences.en: So you've got Leofric in Mercia.
sentences.zh: 所以你有麦西亚的利奥弗里克。

sentences.en: You've got Elfgar in East Anglia.
sentences.zh: 你有东盎格利亚的埃尔夫加。

sentences.en: You have this boat, Seaward in Northumbria.
sentences.zh: 你有诺森布里亚的西瓦德。

sentences.en: And Harold in Wessex.
sentences.zh: 还有威塞克斯的哈罗德。

sentences.en: And Edward can kind of play them off against each other, presumably.
sentences.zh: 爱德华大概可以利用他们相互制衡。

sentences.en: There's a bit of a balance.
sentences.zh: 这是一种平衡。

sentences.en: I'd agree there's kind of balance of power there.
sentences.zh: 我同意那里确实存在一种权力平衡。

sentences.en: But then in 1055, so that's only two years after the death of Godwin, there's another dramatic development because Seward dies, the Earl of Northumbria.
sentences.zh: 但在1055年，也就是戈德温死后仅两年，又发生了一个戏剧性的发展，因为诺森布里亚伯爵西瓦德去世了。

sentences.en: People just keep dying in history, don't they?
sentences.zh: 人们在历史上总是不断地死去，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's the occupational hazard of being an 11th century Earl, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想这是作为11世纪伯爵的职业风险。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the huge question is who is going to succeed Seward as Earl of Northumbria?
sentences.zh: 而最大的问题是谁将接替西瓦德担任诺森布里亚伯爵？

sentences.en: And Harold leans on Edward.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德向爱德华施压。

sentences.en: Edith leans on Edward.
sentences.zh: 伊迪丝向爱德华施压。

sentences.en: And they persuade Edward to appoint to the vacant earldom of Northumbria their brother Tostig.
sentences.zh: 他们说服爱德华任命他们的兄弟托斯蒂格为诺森布里亚伯爵。

sentences.en: And the life of King Edward, unsurprisingly, thinks this is brilliant.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，《爱德华国王传》认为这太棒了。

sentences.en: Good news for Tostig.
sentences.zh: 对托斯蒂格来说是个好消息。

sentences.en: Good news for Northumbria.
sentences.zh: 对诺森布里亚来说是个好消息。

sentences.en: Good news for England.
sentences.zh: 对英国来说是个好消息。

sentences.en: And it does acknowledge that Tostig is a bit shorter than Harold, but insists otherwise that he's quite as brave, quite as strong,
sentences.zh: 它确实承认托斯蒂格比哈罗德稍微矮一点，但坚持认为他在其他方面同样勇敢、同样强壮，

sentences.en: quite as handsome as the absolute paragon that is his elder brother.
sentences.zh: 同样英俊，就像他那作为绝对典范的哥哥一样。

sentences.en: Now, the Godwins obviously think this is tremendous, but there are lots of people who are really opposed to Tostig becoming the Earl of Northumbria.
sentences.zh: 现在，戈德温家族显然认为这太棒了，但有很多人非常反对托斯蒂格成为诺森布里亚伯爵。

sentences.en: So Alfgar, who is the son of Leofric, the Earl of Mercia, who's just been appointed the Earl of East Anglia, he has a massive strop.
sentences.zh: 所以利奥弗里克的儿子、麦西亚伯爵埃尔夫加，他刚刚被任命为东盎格利亚伯爵，他大发雷霆。

sentences.en: He briefly threatens a civil war, goes into exile, comes back, but Harold manages to patch things up with him.
sentences.zh: 他短暂地威胁要发动内战，流亡，又回来，但哈罗德设法与他修补了关系。

sentences.en: In the North, there's a lot of grumbling because Northerners back then, I mean, it's no longer the case, but back then they didn't like Southerners particularly.
sentences.zh: 在北方，有很多抱怨，因为当时的北方人，我的意思是，现在情况已经不同了，但当时他们特别不喜欢南方人。

sentences.en: Yeah, that would never happen now.
sentences.zh: 是的，现在这种情况永远不会发生了。

sentences.en: That would never happen now.
sentences.zh: 现在这种情况永远不会发生了。

sentences.en: And then in 1058, the Godwins are still on manoeuvres.
sentences.zh: 然后在1058年，戈德温家族仍在进行操纵。

sentences.en: So they don't really want Alfgar as Earl of East Anglia.
sentences.zh: 他们并不真正想要埃尔夫加担任东盎格利亚伯爵。

sentences.en: So they elbow him aside and appoint another of Harold's brothers,
sentences.zh: 所以他们把他挤到一边，任命了哈罗德的另一个兄弟，

sentences.en: Girth, to become the Earl of East Anglia.
sentences.zh: 吉尔斯，担任东盎格利亚伯爵。

sentences.en: And Alfgar has another massive strop.
sentences.zh: 埃尔夫加又大发雷霆。

sentences.en: Again, he goes into exile.
sentences.zh: 他又流亡了。

sentences.en: Again, he comes back.
sentences.zh: 他又回来了。

sentences.en: Again, Harold patches things up.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德又修补了关系。

sentences.en: And there's this brilliant comment about it in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle that listeners may well agree with.
sentences.zh: 《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》中对此有一段精彩的评论，听众们可能会非常赞同。

sentences.en: It is tedious to tell how it all happened.
sentences.zh: 讲述这一切是如何发生的真是令人厌烦。

sentences.en: If we adopted that mantra, there'd been definitely no podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 如果我们采纳那句口头禅，那肯定就不会有播客了。

sentences.en: But essentially, there is kind of festering resentment on the part of Leofric, Alfgar, and Alfgar's sons, Edwin and Morkar.
sentences.zh: 但本质上，利奥弗里克、埃尔夫加以及埃尔夫加的儿子们埃德温和莫卡心中确实存在着积怨。

sentences.en: So this kind of this great dynasty in the middle of England.
sentences.zh: 所以这是英格兰中部的一个伟大的王朝。

sentences.en: And they don't like being sandwiched between two of the Godwinsons,
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢被夹在两个戈德温家族成员之间，

sentences.en: Harold in the south, Tostig in the north, and now with the appointment of Girth, the Eldom of East Anglia, to their east as well.
sentences.zh: 南方的哈罗德，北方的托斯蒂格，现在随着吉尔斯的任命，东面还有东盎格利亚伯爵领。

sentences.en: And the life of King Edward obviously thinks it's fantastic.
sentences.zh: 而《爱德华国王传》显然认为这太棒了。

sentences.en: You know, it's wonderful that essentially,
sentences.zh: 你知道，本质上这太美妙了，

sentences.en: England is pretty much now securely Godwin-run.
sentences.zh: 英格兰现在几乎稳固地由戈德温家族统治。

sentences.en: And exclaims, And so with the kingdom made safe on all sides by these nobles, the most kindly King Edward passed his life in security and peace.
sentences.zh: 并惊叹道：因此，随着王国在各方面都由这些贵族保障安全，最仁慈的爱德华国王在安全与和平中度过了一生。

sentences.en: That's lovely.
sentences.zh: 那太美好了。

sentences.en: But obviously, King Edward is not going to last forever.
sentences.zh: 但显然，爱德华国王不可能永远活下去。

sentences.en: And there is this massive question mark about what happens if, assuming, I mean, I think everyone's probably assumed by now, haven't they?
sentences.zh: 而且有一个巨大的问号，关于如果发生什么，假设——我的意思是，我想大家现在可能都已经假设了吧？

sentences.en: He's never going to have a son to succeed him.
sentences.zh: 他永远不会有儿子来继承他。

sentences.en: He and Edith are never going to have children.
sentences.zh: 他和伊迪丝永远不会有孩子。

sentences.en: So the question now is, who comes next?
sentences.zh: 所以现在的问题是，谁来接替？

sentences.en: Because everybody must be thinking this from the mid to late 1050s onwards.
sentences.zh: 因为每个人从1050年代中期到后期一定都在想这个问题。

sentences.en: And as the 1050s turned to the 1060s, the fame of Harold as a warrior grows.
sentences.zh: 随着1050年代进入1060年代，哈罗德作为战士的名声越来越大。

sentences.en: But so also across the channel is the fame of another great warrior,
sentences.zh: 但海峡对岸另一位伟大战士的名声也随之增长，

sentences.en: William the Duke of Normandy.
sentences.zh: 诺曼底公爵威廉。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The fame of Harold is complemented by that of William, and the fame of William is complemented by that of Harold.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德的名声与威廉的名声相辅相成，威廉的名声也与哈罗德的名声相辅相成。

sentences.en: And the sense of them is these two great models of warrior lords.
sentences.zh: 他们被视为战士领主的两个伟大典范。

sentences.en: People know what the implication of this is.
sentences.zh: 人们知道这意味着什么。

sentences.en: You know, there's the prospect of an almighty crash coming.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一场巨大的碰撞即将到来。

sentences.en: So to look at Harold first, his record in the 1060s.
sentences.zh: 首先看看哈罗德，他在1060年代的记录。

sentences.en: In 1062, he launches a surprise attack on this guy called Gruffid Apgluelen, a prince who has made himself king of pretty much the whole of Wales.
sentences.zh: 1062年，他对一个叫格鲁菲德·阿普·卢埃林的人发动了突然袭击，这位王子使自己成为了几乎整个威尔士的国王。

sentences.en: That's a very rare occurrence.
sentences.zh: 那是非常罕见的现象。

sentences.en: Wales is normally very kind of patchwork of rival princedoMs.
sentences.zh: 威尔士通常是非常零散的敌对公国。

sentences.en: But this Gruffid has made himself king of Wales.
sentences.zh: 但这位格鲁菲德使自己成为了威尔士国王。

sentences.en: And this is obviously seen by the English elites as a direct threat to them.
sentences.zh: 这显然被英国精英视为对他们的直接威胁。

sentences.en: And Harold launches a surprise attack.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德发动了突然袭击。

sentences.en: Gruffid is taken completely by surprise.
sentences.zh: 格鲁菲德完全措手不及。

sentences.en: He manages to escape.
sentences.zh: 他设法逃脱了。

sentences.en: But the following year in 1063, he's cornered in the wilds of Snowdonia and decapitated.
sentences.zh: 但第二年，即1063年，他在斯诺多尼亚的荒野中被围困并被斩首。

sentences.en: And his head is sent to Harold, who then sends it on to Edward the Confessor.
sentences.zh: 他的头颅被送往哈罗德那里，哈罗德随后将其转送给忏悔者爱德华。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, across the channel,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在海峡对岸，

sentences.en: William has invaded and successfully annexed Maine, which people who listened to the previous episode may remember,
sentences.zh: 威廉入侵并成功吞并了曼恩，听过上一集的人可能还记得，

sentences.en: is the kind of the border zone between Normandy and the great county of Anjou, the Normans' deadliest enemy, really.
sentences.zh: 那是诺曼底和安茹大伯爵领之间的边界地带，实际上是诺曼人最致命的敌人。

sentences.en: And William has done this in a very brutal and effective way.
sentences.zh: 威廉以一种非常残酷和有效的方式做到了这一点。

sentences.en: And a chronicler in praise of William says, terror was sown across the land.
sentences.zh: 一位赞美威廉的编年史家说，恐怖在整个土地上播种。

sentences.en: And the consequence of this is that
sentences.zh: 而其后果是

sentences.en: William now has nothing to fear from his southern flank.
sentences.zh: 威廉现在不必担心他的南翼了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he can look northwards.
sentences.zh: 所以他可以向北看。

sentences.en: He can be thinking about what happens in England.
sentences.zh: 他可以考虑英格兰会发生什么。

sentences.en: Yes, he absolutely can.
sentences.zh: 是的，他绝对可以。

sentences.en: And so finally, we come to this moment, one of the most famous moments, not just of this whole story, but in all English medieval history.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们来到了这一刻，这是整个故事中最著名的时刻之一，不仅是这个故事，也是整个英国中世纪历史中最著名的时刻之一。

sentences.en: So either in 1064 or in 1065,
sentences.zh: 所以要么是在1064年，要么是在1065年，

sentences.en: Harold and William at last come face to face.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德和威廉终于面对面了。

sentences.en: And it's the very first episode that you see on the Bayer Tapestry.
sentences.zh: 这是你在《贝叶挂毯》上看到的第一个场景。

sentences.en: You know, one of the most famous, I was about to say one of the most famous documents.
sentences.zh: 你知道，最著名的之一，我正要说这是最著名的文献之一。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess it is a document of a kind.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想它确实是一种文献。

sentences.en: One of the most famous documents, not just in English history, but in all history.
sentences.zh: 最著名的文献之一，不仅在英国历史上，而且在整个历史上。

sentences.en: So Tom, tell us how Harold and William finally get to meet.
sentences.zh: 那么汤姆，告诉我们哈罗德和威廉最终是如何见面的。

sentences.en: So as you say, I mean, it is shown on the Bayer Tapestry and there are Norman accounts, there are English accounts.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，我的意思是，它显示在《贝叶挂毯》上，有诺曼人的记载，也有英国人的记载。

sentences.en: The Norman and English accounts often differ quite radically on the spin and interpretation they put on the episode.
sentences.zh: 诺曼人和英国人的记载在他们对这一事件的描述和解释上往往有很大的不同。

sentences.en: But I think the basic outline is clear.
sentences.zh: 但我认为基本轮廓是清楚的。

sentences.en: Essentially, Harold sets sail southwards.
sentences.zh: 总之，哈罗德向南启航了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Why the Bayer Tapestry and the Norman historians insist that he has been sent by Edward to promise William the succession.
sentences.zh: 为什么《贝叶挂毯》和诺曼史学家坚持认为他是受爱德华之命，去向威廉承诺王位继承权的呢？

sentences.en: The English insist that he travelled there of his own volition in order to negotiate a marriage alliance or the release of some hostages of his own family,
sentences.zh: 英国方面则坚持认为，他是自愿前往那里，目的是为了商谈联姻，或者为了营救他家族中的一些人质，

sentences.en: some of his brothers who have been kept by William.
sentences.zh: 也就是他的一些被威廉扣押的兄弟。

sentences.en: William of Malmesbury, the Dominic Sandbrook of the 12th century, suggests that, who's very, very patriotic, suggests that Harold had been blown off course while on a fishing trip.
sentences.zh: 马姆斯伯里的威廉——也就是12世纪的多米尼克·桑德布鲁克，他非常、非常爱国——他认为哈罗德是在一次捕鱼旅行中被风吹离了航线。

sentences.en: Yeah, that sounds the most plausible to me.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这听起来对我来说最合理。

sentences.en: So anyway, what happens then is that whatever reason Harold is sailing southwards across the Channel, he's shipwrecked and he's taken prisoner by a local princeling.
sentences.zh: 总之，无论哈罗德南下穿越海峡的真正原因是什么，他遭遇了海难，并被当地的一位小诸侯俘虏了。

sentences.en: William secures his release.
sentences.zh: 威廉确保了他的获释。

sentences.en: Harold becomes William's gueSt.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德成了威廉的座上宾。

sentences.en: He joins him on a campaign against the Bretons, the kind of the milk-drinking barbarians of Brittany.
sentences.zh: 他加入了威廉针对布列塔尼人的军事行动，那些布列塔尼人就像是喝奶的野蛮人。

sentences.en: And he watches the Normans in action.
sentences.zh: 他观察了诺曼人的作战方式。

sentences.en: He watches their cavalry.
sentences.zh: 他观察了他们的骑兵。

sentences.en: He watches them build their castles.
sentences.zh: 他观察了他们如何建造城堡。

sentences.en: He is able to see their military operations up close.
sentences.zh: 他得以近距离观察他们的军事行动。

sentences.en: And when they're not fighting,
sentences.zh: 当他们不打仗的时候，

sentences.en: William and Harold are talking geopolitics.
sentences.zh: 威廉和哈罗德就在谈论地缘政治。

sentences.en: And it's evident that Harold, who is very charming, very proficient in making people like him, gets William to talk about his ambitions.
sentences.zh: 很明显，哈罗德非常迷人，非常擅长让人喜欢他，他诱使威廉谈论了自己的野心。

sentences.en: William talks about how, you know, he feels he has this right to the English throne.
sentences.zh: 威廉谈到了他如何认为自己有权继承英国王位。

sentences.en: He wants to press it.
sentences.zh: 他想争取这个权利。

sentences.en: He absolutely believes that Edward has promised him the throne.
sentences.zh: 他绝对相信爱德华已经向他承诺了王位。

sentences.en: And Harold then swears an oath on the bones of saints that he will uphold William's claim to the English throne.
sentences.zh: 于是哈罗德在圣徒遗骨上起誓，承诺支持威廉对英国王位的要求。

sentences.en: And again, Norman historians insist he does this because Edward has sent him to do it.
sentences.zh: 同样，诺曼史学家坚持认为他这样做是因为爱德华派他去的。

sentences.en: Yeah, because he was always going to do it.
sentences.zh: 是啊，因为他本来就打算这么做。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: An English historian say that basically he couldn't see any way of escape without agreeing to all that William wished.
sentences.zh: 一位英国史学家说，基本上他看不出除了同意威廉想要的一切之外，还有什么逃脱的方法。

sentences.en: William basically forces him to do it.
sentences.zh: 威廉基本上是强迫他这么做的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, he doesn't have any other way of getting back.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他没有其他办法回国了。

sentences.en: Otherwise, he'll be a kind of hostage in Normandy.
sentences.zh: 否则，他就会成为诺曼底的人质。

sentences.en: So he does this.
sentences.zh: 所以他照做了。

sentences.en: He swears to uphold William's right to the English throne.
sentences.zh: 他发誓支持威廉对英国王位的权利。

sentences.en: And he is then given a Norman ship.
sentences.zh: 然后他得到了一艘诺曼船。

sentences.en: It's loaded down with gifts.
sentences.zh: 船上装满了礼物。

sentences.en: And Harold sails back to England.
sentences.zh: 哈罗德航行回到了英国。

sentences.en: And so the huge question hanging over this is, you know, what is the truth?
sentences.zh: 所以，悬在这件事上的巨大疑问是，真相到底是什么？

sentences.en: What had Harold been up to?
sentences.zh: 哈罗德到底在搞什么名堂？

sentences.en: And Edward A.
sentences.zh: 爱德华·A·弗里曼，

sentences.en: Freeman, the Regist Professor of Oxford in the 19th century, who wrote, again, a kind of Sandbrookian six-volume history of the Norman conquest, he said of this,
sentences.zh: 19世纪牛津大学的雷吉乌斯教授，他写了一部类似于桑德布鲁克风格的六卷本诺曼征服史，他对此评价道：

sentences.en: It is one of the most perplexing questions in all history.
sentences.zh: 这是历史上最令人困惑的问题之一。

sentences.en: I don't know whether you agree with that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否同意这一点。

sentences.en: It's not wrong.
sentences.zh: 这评价没错。

sentences.en: So here's the thing, right?
sentences.zh: 所以问题就在这儿，对吧？

sentences.en: I think you and I probably agree on this.
sentences.zh: 我想你和我可能对此有共识。

sentences.en: And we agree, Will, so with other recent historians.
sentences.zh: 威尔，我们和其他近期的史学家看法一致。

sentences.en: So, for example, Mark Morris, who's written about the Norman conquest and the end of Anglo-Saxon England.
sentences.zh: 比如，写过关于诺曼征服和盎格鲁-撒克逊英格兰终结的马克·莫里斯。

sentences.en: It's just utterly implausible that Harold, who is so powerful and rich and such a serious player, would have meekly crossed the channel
sentences.zh: 哈罗德如此强大、富有，是一个如此重要的角色，他竟然会顺从地穿越海峡，

sentences.en: in response to Edward the Confessor's instructions to swear allegiance to the Duke of Normandy.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了响应忏悔者爱德华的指示去向诺曼底公爵宣誓效忠，这简直太不可思议了。

sentences.en: I mean, that just seems absolutely unbelievable, doesn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这看起来绝对令人难以置信，不是吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: But then, of course, there is the question of, well, why does he go?
sentences.zh: 但当然，问题在于，他为什么要走呢？

sentences.en: You know, and the claim of English historians that he's going to negotiate the release of his brothers, I mean, it's perfectly possible.
sentences.zh: 你知道，英国史学家声称他是去商谈营救他的兄弟，这完全是有可能的。

sentences.en: Yeah, there are historians who think that, who say, if he wanted to succeed, then having these hostages at the Norman court would have been a massive time bomb.
sentences.zh: 是啊，有些史学家认为，如果他想继位，那么让这些兄弟作为人质留在诺曼宫廷将是一个巨大的定时炸弹。

sentences.en: So he wants to get them back.
sentences.zh: 所以他想把他们接回来。

sentences.en: But also it's humiliating for his family to have hostages at the Norman court.
sentences.zh: 而且让家人作为人质留在诺曼宫廷对他家族来说也是一种羞辱。

sentences.en: Yeah, so there is that.
sentences.zh: 是啊，确实有这方面原因。

sentences.en: But I think, I still don't think that is adequate to explain why he would put himself in such a risky situation.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这仍然不足以解释他为何要让自己陷入如此危险的境地。

sentences.en: And I think the answer is, again, is to be found in the life of King Edward, full of gems and riches.
sentences.zh: 我认为答案再次可以在充满珍宝和财富的《爱德华国王传》中找到。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it gives an account of a pilgrimage that Harold made to Rome kind of earlier in the 1050s, which very clearly simultaneously served as a kind of espionage mission.
sentences.zh: 书中记载了哈罗德在1050年代早期前往罗马的一次朝圣，这显然同时充当了一种间谍任务。

sentences.en: So to quote the life of King Edward, he studied the character, policy and strength of the princes of Gaul, not only through his servants,
sentences.zh: 引用《爱德华国王传》的话，他研究了高卢诸侯的性格、政策和实力，不仅通过他的仆人，

sentences.en: but in person and adroitly and with natural cunning and with lengthy and intent observation.
sentences.zh: 而且是亲力亲为，机敏地、带着天生的狡黠以及漫长而专注的观察。

sentences.en: So that's not written about Harold's trip to Normandy.
sentences.zh: 所以那并不是关于哈罗德去诺曼底的旅行。

sentences.en: The life of King Edward doesn't really mention that.
sentences.zh: 《爱德华国王传》并没有真正提到那次旅行。

sentences.en: But it's clear that this is part of Harold's policy.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，这是哈罗德政策的一部分。

sentences.en: He believes in good intelligence.
sentences.zh: 他相信情报的重要性。

sentences.en: And I suppose because he rates his own powers of observation, he wants to see it for himself.
sentences.zh: 我想因为他对自己观察力的自信，他想亲眼看看。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I suspect that he's going to try and get his brothers back.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑他确实是想把他的兄弟们接回来。

sentences.en: But above all, he's doing it because he wants to spy out the Norman way of war.
sentences.zh: 但最重要的是，他这样做是因为他想刺探诺曼人的战争方式。

sentences.en: Most people in England have no awareness of the kind of military revolution that is occurring.
sentences.zh: 英国的大多数人对正在发生的军事革命毫无察觉。

sentences.en: But Harold obviously does because he's been to France and he's seen it.
sentences.zh: 但哈罗德显然知道，因为他去过法国，他亲眼见识过。

sentences.en: And he wants to see how this revolution is operating specifically in the context of Normandy.
sentences.zh: 他想看看这场革命具体在诺曼底是如何运作的。

sentences.en: He wants to see how the Duke's castles are built, the aggressive use to which they can be put, the potential of the Norman cavalry.
sentences.zh: 他想看看公爵的城堡是如何建造的，它们能被用于何种侵略性用途，以及诺曼骑兵的潜力。

sentences.en: And the problem for Harold, of course, is that to extract himself from the spy mission, he does clearly have to swear this oath.
sentences.zh: 当然，哈罗德的问题在于，为了从间谍任务中脱身，他显然必须发下这个誓言。

sentences.en: I mean, everyone, essentially English as well as Norman, accept this.
sentences.zh: 我是说，每个人，本质上无论是英国人还是诺曼人，都接受这一点。

sentences.en: But I guess he would say, you know, needs muSt.

sentences.en: And you can, of course, hear both of those episodes at once by signing up to The Rest Is History Club at therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 当然，您可以通过注册 therestishistory.com 的“历史其余部分俱乐部”一次性收听这两集节目。

sentences.en: That's right, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 没错，多米尼克。

sentences.en: And then when we've done that, we will be back with the story of 1066 itself.
sentences.zh: 做完这些之后，我们将回归讲述1066年本身的故事。

sentences.en: The invasion led by Harold Hardrada, and then the invasion led by William Duke of Normandy.
sentences.zh: 由哈拉尔·哈德拉达领导的入侵，以及随后由诺曼底公爵威廉领导的入侵。

sentences.en: So, lots more to come.
sentences.zh: 所以，还有很多精彩内容。

sentences.en: But in the meanwhile, thanks very much for listening.
sentences.zh: 但在此期间，非常感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
